title: Finite isomorphisms lift above fixed stage objects
statement: Let J be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], F : J → Cat a strict diagram, and V a cocone whose object and arrow cocones [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor] are colimits of sets. Fix a finite index type I, a stage j, objects D_i in F(j), objects Z_i in V.pt, and isomorphisms E_i : V_j(D_i) ≅ Z_i. There exist a stage k, a transition c : j → k, objects D′_i in F(k), and isomorphisms t_i : D′_i ≅ F(c)(D_i), such that the image arrow of t_i.hom equals E_i.inv as an Arrow, including both endpoints. No precoverage or pullback assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 09YL, finite-diagram observation; Categories Tag 04AX, eventual equality

proof.text: Apply joint surjectivity of the arrow cocone to the hom and inverse of each E_i. Move this finite family above j using IsFiltered.wideSpan and maxima. The images of the inverse targets and hom sources equal the images of F(c)(D_i), and the images of the hom targets equal those of the inverse sources. Apply eventual object equality simultaneously, using wideSpan, to align these three endpoint equations for each i. Transport the arrows along these equations.

Cocone naturality preserves the prescribed Arrow images after transport. Equality of Arrow images respects composition, so the two composites have the same Arrow images as the appropriate identities. Apply eventual equality in the arrow colimit to both equations for every i and synchronize the refinements by IsFiltered.wideSpan.

Functoriality turns the resulting Arrow equalities into inverse equations. Construct the stage isomorphisms from the two maps and transport their codomains along F.map_comp to the image under the composite transition j → m. Cocone naturality and invariance of Arrow.mk under endpoint transport give exactly the prescribed inverse images. The finite-family helpers also handle the empty family, using the given stage j.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09YL, finite-diagram observation; Categories Tag 04AX, eventual equality; Lean proof by H1 second reader directly from the set-colimit criteria and IsFiltered.wideSpan

mathlib_searches.query: lift finite family of isomorphisms above a fixed stage in a filtered colimit of categories
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits inspected: Ind.exists_nonempty_arrow_mk_iso_ind_lim, eventual-constant cocone isomorphisms, filtered set equality and IsFiltered.sup_exists. None lifts a finite family of category isomorphisms above prescribed stage objects.
Twelve hits inspected, including IsPullback.isoIsPullback and of_iso′. These supply comparison and transport and are used in the item, but do not lift their finite family above a fixed stage.

Mathlib general search returned unrelated finite-limit and algebra hits. Focused local search found filteredColimit_category_iso_clause: a single arbitrary-stage isomorphism for the canonical object colimit, conditional on finite-functor lifting. It does not provide finite simultaneous lifting above prescribed stage objects. FiniteLift, FiniteFunctorLift and ListEquality likewise have canonical-colimit signatures, not this arbitrary-cocone conclusion. No exact upstream or Sheaf declaration.

lean.statement:
theorem filteredColimit_finite_iso_lift
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (V : Cocone F) (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (j : J) (D : ι → F.obj j) (Z : ι → V.pt)
    (E : ∀ i, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj (D i) ≅ Z i) :
    ∃ (k : J) (c : j ⟶ k) (D' : ι → F.obj k)
      (t : ∀ i, D' i ≅ (F.map c).toFunctor.obj (D i)),
      ∀ i, Arrow.mk ((V.ι.app k).toFunctor.map (t i).hom) = Arrow.mk (E i).inv
